chunks: Ahmad, from ʿAbd al-ʿAẓīm, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Mayyāḥ, from the one who informed him, who said:
A man recited in the presence of Abī ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام).
“Say: Work, so Allah will see your deeds, and His Messenger, and the believers.”
So he (عليه السلام) said: “It is not like this; rather, it is: ‘and the trusted ones.’”

key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abū ʿAbdillāh, the Imam Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq (عليه السلام)
key_terms.اللَّهُ: Allah, Who sees and knows human actions
key_terms.الْمَأْمُونُونَ: the trusted or entrusted ones, identified here as the Imams (عليهم السلام)
key_terms.الْمُؤْمِنُونَ: the believers, as recited in the verse
key_terms.رَسُولُهُ: His Messenger, the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

ai.seo_question: Who are the ones referred to as witnesses over people’s deeds in Qur'an 9:105 according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith presents a reading connected to Qur'anic interpretation in which Imam Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام) identifies “the trusted ones” as those referred to in the verse. The report highlights a Shia understanding of wilayah and the special authority of the Imams (عليهم السلام) in relation to divine witness over human deeds.
